Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Deployed and verified.

**URL: https://umami-acsa19243a7-299813327652.us-central1.run.app** — HTTP 200, `/api/heartbeat` returns `{"ok":true}`, page title `Umami`.

## What was deployed (GCP only — the redu/AWS/Azure notes in the folder were ignored)

Project `redu-425516`, region `us-central1`:

| Resource | Name |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run service | `umami-acsa19243a7` (token in hostname, used nowhere else) |
| Artifact Registry repo | `acsa19243a7` — mirror of the umami image |
| Cloud SQL Postgres 16 | `umami-pg-sess0901`, db-f1-micro, database `umami` |

- **Image:** the compose file's digest pin `docker.umami.is/umami-software/umami@sha256:fa32d116…`. Per the notes I re-resolved `postgresql-latest` before deploying — it still points at that same digest — then mirrored it into Artifact Registry, since Cloud Run can't pull from `docker.umami.is`.
- **Database:** real Cloud SQL instance, reached over the Cloud Run Cloud SQL socket (`?host=/cloudsql/redu-425516:us-central1:umami-pg-sess0901`), not an ephemeral sidecar — Umami's Prisma migrations ran on first boot. I chose this over an in-instance Postgres because a Cloud Run instance's local DB would be wiped on every cold start and would diverge across instances.
- **Config:** port 3000, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB, min-instances 1, max 4, startup CPU boost, unauthenticated access, explicit `APP_SECRET` so sessions survive a DB credential change (per the compose file's intent).

## Credentials — store these, they are not written to any file in the repo

- Umami admin: `admin` / `[REDACTED:value]`
- `APP_SECRET`: `[REDACTED:value]` (pass the same value on every redeploy)
- Cloud SQL `postgres` password: `[REDACTED:value]`

The documented default login (`admin`/`umami`) was live from the moment the container went healthy, so I rotated it immediately via `POST /api/me/password` and confirmed it: the old default now returns 401, the new password returns 200.

Two standing-cost notes: the Cloud SQL instance bills continuously (~$9/mo for db-f1-micro) regardless of traffic, unlike the usage-metered Cloud Run service, and `min-instances=1` keeps one Cloud Run instance warm rather than scaling to zero. Deleting the Cloud Run service alone will not stop either charge — the SQL instance and the Artifact Registry repo need separate deletion.
